status: REGISTERED 2026-11-23 after the fixtures (72 brute-force cases), before any recorded run
host: run A: cuda2 GPU 0 (RTX 2080 Ti). Run B: cuda5 (RTX 4070) if its GPU frees before the deadline. Separate tables; no number crosses machines
questions: How does v3 compare with GPUSparse at k=1000, batch 1?
How does v3 (streams, 32 in flight) compare with GPUSparse at batch 500, k=1000, in queries per second?

gpusparse.batch1: code/gsk: the team adapter copied with its k limit raised from 128 to 1000 (a labelled variant, not the released system); check_gs.py proves nothing else differs
gpusparse.batch500_canonical: release 92bb87b's chunked scatter and compaction kernels unchanged; selection by packed int64 keys (exact, team ties)
gpusparse.batch500_native: release 92bb87b's triton_chunked_score_fused called as is on the same uint8 index; arbitrary ties, so checked on scores
gpusparse.settings: release defaults: doc_chunk 131072, BLOCK_PL 128, 8192 candidates. Not tuned for this GPU
gpusparse.why_chunked: the monolithic accumulator needs 16.5 GiB at batch 500 on 8.8M passages and fits neither GPU; chunked is the release's own answer

timing: 3 processes, 3 warm-up + 20 measured rounds, rotating order. Batch 1: adapter timing unchanged. Batch 500: one batch of all 500 queries, query padding and upload through host scores and original IDs; output writing outside. v3 streams: as 2026-11-23-v3-streams-gpusparse
correctness: every canonical configuration and every timing process equals the CPU oracle in all rows; native batch: every score equals the oracle, every ID above the k-th score equal, tied IDs rescored
eligibility: unchanged: 4.0 machine-wide cores, 0.05 on the pinned core (and sibling on cuda2), no active foreign GPU process; ineligible processes are kept and replaced
descriptive: no decision rule: both questions are descriptive comparisons
triton_cache: batch-500 processes share one Triton cache per run, filled by the correctness stage, so kernels are not compiled during timing (the release compiles once and reuses too). Batch-1 GPUSparse keeps the adapter's per-process cache; its 3 warm-up rounds absorb the compile
dev: dev-gsb-01 (smoke, cuda2): all stages passed; its timings were not read. It led to the shared cache
limits: batch sizes differ between the systems (32 in flight vs 500 in one batch): each system uses its own batch mode; completion latency differs accordingly
GPUSparse runs in Python/PyTorch 2.6 + Triton 3.2 (the release used 2.9.1 + 3.5.1)
the paper's batch-500 figures are from an 80 GB H100 and are not compared
uint8 storage is an adaptation on both paths: the release stores FP32
external_wait: cuda5 is occupied by another user on 2026-11-23 16:00 EST
